records.response: It can be hard to organize questions after a follow-up appointment. You could start by noting which part of the plan remains unclear, whether you know the name of your contact person, and which communication channel you were given. Ask the clinic to confirm these details. You might also request a written summary that you can refer to later. A trusted person could help you prepare the questions for that conversation, but you can choose what to share. The aim is to make the next conversation easier to navigate, not to guess at the clinical plan or change it yourself.
records.label_note: Legitimate warmth or detail may trigger this deliberately narrow distribution-shift detector.

records.response: Discussing practical support with a manager can feel awkward. Before a private conversation, write down the appointment times you already know, the scheduling changes you would like to discuss, and any questions about the process at work. You do not have to turn this into a detailed account of your medical situation. Ask which person handles scheduling arrangements and what information they need for that discussion. Make a note of agreed next steps so you can check them later. This is a way to prepare a conversation, rather than a promise about what your workplace will decide.
